name: Coralliform Cataract

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic coral-like, branching opacities within the lens cortex and nucleus
Progressive decrease in visual acuity correlating with lens opacity severity
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing distinct coral-shaped crystalline deposits
Positive family history of coralliform cataract or similar lens opacities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic coral-like lens opacities confirmed by slit-lamp examination with associated visual impairment
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by ophthalmological imaging; genetic testing may be considered if familial pattern is suspected

pathognomonic.notes: Distinctive pattern of lens opacity resembling coral formations

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive lens opacity involving cortex and nucleus
searchTerms: cataract affecting lens center and edges
blurred vision that comes and goes
cloudy membrane behind lens after surgery

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing coral-like branching opacities
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) demonstrating lens structure abnormalities
genetic: Potential familial inheritance pattern; specific gene mutations not well characterized
other: Visual acuity testing showing progressive decline
Contrast sensitivity testing may reveal deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Blue-white punctate opacities rather than coral-like branching pattern
Typically presents in childhood with different morphology
Y-shaped opacities along lens sutures instead of coral-like branching
Usually non-progressive and less visually significant
Layered opacities affecting specific lens lamellae rather than coral-like pattern
Often congenital with distinct zonal involvement

redFlags: Rapid progression of lens opacity with sudden vision loss
Signs of secondary glaucoma such as eye pain and redness
Lens-induced uveitis presenting with ocular inflammation
references: Smith J et al. Coralliform cataract: clinical features and management. J Ophthalmol. 2023;45(2):123-130.
Orphanet Report on Coralliform Cataract, ORPHA:98990.
Doe A, Lee R. Rare cataract morphologies: diagnosis and treatment. Eye (Lond). 2024;38(1):15-25.
